harness-maturity-analysis · phase 1E showcase

Does the score
hold up?

2186 of 2186 pinned repositories, one deterministic scanner, one question: when harness-score calls a repository L4 or L0, does it hold up? A high reading measures a repository's harness — never the competence of the company that owns it. This collection supplies scanner evidence; independent blind human ratings are still pending. Includes 30 new AI software projects selected by GitHub stars. Selection and software eligibility. Includes 25 cryptocurrency software projects selected by accumulated GitHub stars. Crypto selection and software eligibility. Media editing cohort selection: 25 projects from a recorded bounded GitHub search union. Selection and source evidence. Includes 500 video game AI and AI-assisted game development projects selected by stars within a bounded search union. Selection and source evidence. Includes 1000 new public software repositories selected by GitHub stars within a bounded search union. Popularity is selection metadata, not maturity. Selection and source evidence.

harness-score@1.8.1 2186/2186 repositories scanned zero LLM calls, zero network at scan time source on GitHub →

The leaderboard

Every bar is one pinned commit scanned with the pinned tool version. Bar length is total score; color is the gated maturity level — they can diverge, and where they do is the most interesting part of this study. Full raw data: leaderboard.csv.

observation from the original 21-repository analysis

Anthropic's skills showcase shares L0 with a minimal repo

anthropic/skills — Anthropic's official showcase of Claude Skills — scores L0 · 16%, sharing a maturity level with octocat/Hello-World. Its skills live at skills/<name>/SKILL.md (repository root) rather than .claude/skills/, because this repository distributes skills rather than using them to develop itself — and the relevant check correctly answers the question it's built to ask ("does this repo have a self-referential skill harness?") with "no." The original 1.5.0 analysis identified a category gap for canonical artifact collections, including the root .claude-plugin/ manifest. This historical finding has not been revalidated as a model critique for the expanded cohort.

resolved in harness-score 1.5.0

HKS-05 now recognizes both corpus regressions

On the same pinned commits, cline moves from 78 to 80 points and promptfoo moves from 95 to 97. Their HKS-05 checks now pass: unbraced environment-variable paths and dependency-managed binaries are both resolved correctly. The original diagnosis remains documented in analysis/findings.md.

How much of the score is actually "AI harness"?

Splitting each report's earned points into AI-specific (Context + Skills + Hooks) versus generic engineering hygiene (Sensors + CI + Hygiene) distinguishes agent artifacts from conventional engineering signals. gpt-researcher has 2% AI-specific share and scores 51% overall. The original 21-repository interpretation is in analysis/findings.md.

WHAT THIS DOESN'T CLAIM

Not whether the tests are good, whether the rules are true, or whether the team practices code review. A high reading means the infrastructure for reliable agent work exists. Necessary, not sufficient. Full framing in METHODOLOGY.md.

PHASE STATUS

  1. Pipeline scaffold, validated against 4 anchors
  2. Corpus frozen: 2186/2186 repositories scanned
  3. Blind human ratings — needs a rater, not an agent
  4. Q2 model-calibration synthesis — 7 findings, 4 proposals
